inspiration: Per-cell ownership field: the engine reports, for each board cell, a prediction from -1 to 1 of who will own it, and can also report one for each candidate move (docs/Analysis_Engine.md lines 91-93). Keep the one-number-per-cell field drawn as heat; change it into zone-control heat for our arena, with a different palette and an outline for the zone edge.

Expected score alongside win chance: the engine reports both a win-rate style number and an estimate of the expected score (README.md line 243). Keep two readouts for one state: how likely, and how much. Change it into a fight readout with win chance plus expected damage swing.

Cost warning on the heat field: the ownership option doubles memory use and slightly lowers speed (docs/Analysis_Engine.md line 91). Keep the switch that makes the expensive layer opt-in; use the same rule for any heavy HUD overlay on phones.

Rank-shaped opponent: the human-style mode imitates play at a stated rank instead of playing the strongest move (README.md lines 149-154; cpp/configs/gtp_human5k_example.cfg). Keep the idea of an opponent whose mistakes look human; change it into a style-based opponent with three readable tells.

Per-move preview: the analysis can report ownership for each candidate move too (docs/Analysis_Engine.md line 93). Keep the per-option read-out; change it into a per-attack damage-zone preview on hover or long-press.

Curated bad-case lists: misc/badgogodgames holds lists of games the engine handles badly (names only, not read). Keep the idea of a named regression list of known bad scenarios for our fight tests; change the content to our own fight situations.

briefs.label: Zone-control heat overlay
briefs.why: A single number per cell drawn as a gradient makes control of an area readable at a glance, which suits a crowded arena at 375 wide.
briefs.keep: one value per cell from -1 to 1; cool to warm colour ramp; opt-in layer
briefs.change: our own two-colour ramp for two factions; an outline on the zone edge; drawn only in a debug or tactics mode
briefs.ref: docs/Analysis_Engine.md lines 91-93 (ownership option and per-move ownership); README.md line 243

briefs.label: Human-paced opponent with visible tells
briefs.why: An opponent that errs in human-looking places feels fair, and a fight can be tuned to a rank without changing the search.
briefs.keep: imitate a stated level; mistakes come from the level, not from random noise
briefs.change: the level is a fighting style with three named tells, not a rank; the tells are our own animations

briefs.label: Two-number fight readout
briefs.why: Showing a chance and a size side by side tells the player both whether to press and how much it is worth.
briefs.keep: a probability next to a magnitude for the same state
briefs.change: win chance and expected damage swing in our HUD; our own labels and colours
briefs.ref: README.md line 243 (expected score next to winrate)
